title: Railway RRB Section Controller CEN 04/2025 CBAT Exam City Details 2026 Out for 368 Post
intro: Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)  has Officially Released CBAT Exam City/ Admit Card for the Post of Section Controller (CEN. No. 04/2025) Recruitment 2025 for 368 Post. CBAT Exam Held On June 6, 2026 & CBAT Admit Card Released On May, 2026. All Interested Candidate Can Download CBAT Exam City/ Admit Card Now in The Given Link Below

Email: rrb.help@csc.gov.in
Phone:9592001188 / 01725653333 ((10:00AM to 5:00 PM on all working days)
Total Duration: 120 minutes.
Total Questions: 100 objective-type questions with multiple choices.
Negative Marking: There will be negative marking, with a penalty of 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer.
Normalization: The CBT will be held in multiple shifts, and a normalized score will be used for shortlisting candidates for the CBAT.

Mathematics: Includes topics like Averages, Percentages, Profit, Loss & Discounts, Time, Speed, Distance, Power & Work, Algebra, Linear Equations, Arithmetic Progression, LCM, HCF, Geometry, Area & Volumes, Probability & Statistics (both basic level).

Data Analysis & Interpretation: Includes Multi-source Data Analysis, Examination, analysis and Inference drawing from text, tabular data and data represented graphically (charts, graphs, scatter plot, pie chart, statistical curve distribution, Venn Diagrams), Data Sufficiency, and Data Arrangement.
Logical Reasoning: Includes Binary Logic, Syllogism, Clocks & Calendars, Assumptions, Blood Relations, Family Tree, and Solving logic-based puzzles.

Reading Comprehension: Passages would be given from subjects like History, Society, Literature, Science, Environment, Abstract, Mythology, Technology and Culture. Candidates will need to understand the main idea, supporting idea, application, logical structure, and style of the passage to answer questions.
Analogy: Identifying the relationship between two terms and applying it to another pair.
Series Completion: Identifying the pattern in a sequence of numbers and predicting the next term.
Solving Coding-Decoding type questions, Solving Ranking and Arrangements based problems.
Analytical and Mathematical Capability: 60 questions
Logical Capability: 20 questions
Mental Reasoning: 20 questions
Total: 100 questions
Shortlisting: Candidates equal to 8 times the number of vacancies will be selected for the CBAT.
Qualifying Marks: Candidates must secure a minimum T-Score of 42 in each of the test batteries to qualify. This applies to all candidates, regardless of community or category.
Exam Type: This test contains questions and answer options only in English and Hindi.
Negative Marking: There will be no negative marking in the CBAT.
Merit List: The merit list will be drawn based on the candidates' performance in both the CBT (70% weightage) and the CBAT (30% weightage).
Candidates will be called for document verification based on the merit list prepared using a 70% weightage for marks obtained in CBT and a 30% weightage for marks obtained in CBAT.
In case of a tie in marks, the merit position will be determined by age (the older person is placed higher) and then by the alphabetical order of the name.
UR (Unreserved) & EWS (Economically Weaker Section): 40%
OBC (Non-creamy layer): 30%
SC (Scheduled Caste): 30%
ST (Scheduled Tribe): 25%
